I've been working this land for 50 years. My father taught me, and I've learned what this soil needs. Five mu, same fields doing wheat then maize every year — that's the way it's always been in Quzhou. Some of my grandchildren are working in the city now, so I have to manage most of this myself, or hire a machine for the heavy work. At 68, I can't be digging everything by hand anymore.

For the wheat coming up this autumn, I'll rotary till after the maize comes off in September. I'll put in a good improved variety — the county station has been pushing Jimai 22 and I've had decent results with it. I'll apply base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress at jointing in spring. I irrigate the wheat four times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain filling. If I skip one of those my yield drops badly. Aphids and powdery mildew show up every year so I'll spray twice.

For summer maize, I direct seed right after the wheat combine comes through in June. No time to waste — every day matters for the growing season. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or similar — traditional varieties can't match the yield, everyone knows that. I'll put down base fertilizer at planting and topdress once when the plants are knee high. Irrigation depends on rain but I plan for three times with my well. Corn borer and armyworm I watch for — two sprays should handle it.

My goal is around 490 kg/mu on wheat and 580 on maize. That's what I've been getting in good years.
